chart-stacked-bar.context: Three vertical bars on a baseline, each split into a solid lower segment and a thinner upper segment. Used for showing how parts add up to a total across categories in reports and dashboards.

chart-grouped-bar.context: Two clusters of three vertical bars of different heights standing side by side. Used for comparing several series within each category, such as sales by region for each quarter.

chart-percent-stacked-bar.context: Four full height bars, each split at a different point into a solid lower part and a thin upper part. Used for comparing percentage shares across categories when every bar totals 100 percent.

chart-diverging-bar.context: A vertical centre axis with horizontal bars reaching left and right by different amounts. Used for survey agreement scales, gains versus losses and comparisons around a neutral midpoint.

chart-lollipop.context: Four thin stems of different heights on a baseline, each topped with a round marker. Used as a lighter alternative to a bar chart for rankings and comparisons.

chart-dumbbell.context: Three rows beside a vertical axis, each a line joining two markers at different positions. Used for showing the gap or change between two values, such as before and after or two groups.

chart-bullet.context: A horizontal band with a short solid measure bar inside it and a vertical target line crossing it. Used on dashboards to show performance against a goal in a compact space.

chart-marimekko.context: A square split into columns of different widths, each divided into stacked cells of different heights. Used for market share maps where both width and height carry values.

chart-waffle.context: A square grid of nine cells where the bottom row and one more cell hold solid squares. Used to show a percentage or part of a whole as counted squares.

chart-pictogram.context: Two rows of small person figures, all solid except one outlined figure at the end. Used in infographics to show a share of people, such as one in six.

chart-stacked-area.context: Two layered areas rising left to right over a corner axis, separated by a dividing line. Used for showing how several series add up to a total over time.

chart-streamgraph.context: Three flowing wavy bands stacked together with changing thickness and no straight baseline. Used for showing how many categories rise and fall over time.

chart-ridgeline.context: Three hill shaped curves drawn one below another on offset baselines. Used for comparing the distribution of a value across several groups or time periods.

chart-violin.context: Two symmetrical violin shaped outlines side by side, each with a short median line across its widest part. Used in statistics to compare the spread and shape of distributions.

chart-box-plot.context: Two box and whisker plots: boxes with a median line and T shaped whiskers above and below. Used for summarising the range, quartiles and outliers of a data set.

chart-sparkline.context: A small jagged line ending in a dot on the right, inside a slim rounded frame. Used for tiny inline trend charts in tables, cards and dashboards.

chart-combo.context: Three vertical bars with a line of markers running across their tops. Used when one chart shows two kinds of data, such as revenue bars and a growth rate line.

chart-pareto.context: Four bars falling in height from left to right under a curve that rises and levels off near the top. Used for quality analysis to find the few causes behind most problems.

chart-polar-area.context: A round chart of six equal angle wedges that reach out to different lengths from the centre. Used for comparing categories in a circle, such as values by month.

chart-radial-bar.context: Three concentric arcs starting at the top and ending at different lengths around the circle. Used for circular progress bars and comparing a few values in a compact ring layout.

chart-sunburst.context: A circle with an inner pie of three segments and an outer ring split into finer segments that line up with them. Used for showing hierarchical data level by level.

chart-chord.context: A circle with arc segments around its rim and curved ribbons crossing the inside to connect them. Used for showing flows or relationships between groups, such as migration or trade.

chart-arc-diagram.context: A row of dots on a horizontal line joined by arcs of different sizes above it. Used for showing connections between items laid out in order, such as links in a network.

chart-parallel-coordinates.context: Four vertical axes side by side with zigzag lines crossing between them. Used for comparing items across many variables at once in data analysis.

chart-slope.context: Two vertical axes with three straight lines joining dots on the left axis to dots on the right. Used for showing change between two points in time or two conditions.

chart-bump.context: Three lines crossing each other as they move between ranked positions, with a marker at every step. Used for showing how rankings change over time, like league positions.

chart-heatmap.context: A square grid of cells where some hold large solid squares, some small squares and some are empty. Used for showing intensity or values across two categories as a matrix.

chart-circle-packing.context: A large circle holding three smaller solid circles of different sizes. Used for showing hierarchies or sizes of groups as packed bubbles.

chart-dendrogram.context: A tree of right angled brackets joining leaves at the bottom into branches that meet in one line at the top. Used for clustering results, family trees of data and taxonomies.

chart-quadrant.context: A square split into four quadrants by crossed axes, with dots scattered in each part. Used for priority matrices, positioning maps and two by two frameworks.

scatter-plot-matrix.context: A two by two grid of panels: the diagonal panels hold small bars and the others hold scattered dots. Used for comparing every pair of variables in a data set at once.

correlation-matrix.context: A staircase shaped grid of cells, each holding a circle of a different size. Used for showing how strongly pairs of variables relate to each other.

chart-control.context: A zigzag line of points running between two dashed limit lines at the top and bottom. Used in quality control to see whether a process stays within its limits.

chart-ohlc.context: Three vertical price bars, each with a short tick to the left for the open price and one to the right for the close. Used in trading charts for stocks, currencies and commodities.

chart-renko.context: Three hollow bricks stepping diagonally upward, followed by one solid brick stepping down. Used in trading to show price moves of a fixed size while ignoring time.

chart-point-and-figure.context: Columns of stacked X marks on both sides of a column of O marks. Used in technical analysis where X columns show rising prices and O columns show falling prices.

chart-confidence-band.context: A centre line inside a band that grows wider toward the right, over a corner axis. Used for showing uncertainty around an estimate, such as a confidence interval.

chart-error-bars.context: Three vertical bars, each with an I shaped whisker across its top. Used in science and statistics to show the uncertainty or spread around each value.

chart-regression.context: Scattered dots around a straight line rising across a corner axis. Used for showing a trend or relationship fitted to data, such as linear regression.

chart-density.context: A single smooth hill shaped area rising from a flat baseline. Used for showing where values are concentrated in a distribution.

chart-timeline.context: A horizontal line with three dots and flag shaped labels branching alternately above and below. Used for chronologies, project milestones, history pages and roadmaps.

chart-fishbone.context: A fish skeleton diagram: a horizontal spine ending in a box head, with diagonal bones above and below. Used in root cause analysis to group the causes of a problem.

chart-burnup.context: A corner axis with a dashed scope line near the top and a jagged line climbing up toward it. Used in agile teams to track completed work against total scope.

chart-cohort.context: A staircase shaped table of cells that go from solid on the left, to small squares, to empty on the right. Used for retention analysis that follows groups of users over time.

chart-word-cloud.context: A cloud outline holding short bars of different weights like words of different sizes. Used for text analysis, keyword summaries and survey comments.

chart-beeswarm.context: Rows of dots packed side by side along a horizontal line, thicker where many values cluster. Used for showing every data point of a distribution without overlap.

chart-dot-plot.context: Columns of stacked dots of different heights standing on a baseline. Used for counting how often each value occurs, like a histogram made of dots.

chart-spiral.context: A line spiralling out from the centre with dots marked along it. Used for showing time based data that repeats in cycles, such as seasons or days of the week.

chart-ternary.context: A triangle with three inner grid lines parallel to its sides and a few dots plotted inside. Used for mixtures of three parts, such as soil types, alloys or votes split three ways.

chart-3d-bar.context: Three box shaped bars shown in perspective, rising in height from left to right. Used for three dimensional bar charts in presentations and reports.

chart-pie-3d.context: A tilted pie chart drawn as an ellipse with visible thickness at the front and slice lines on top. Used for three dimensional pie charts in presentations and reports.

chart-dual-axis.context: A frame with tick marks on both the left and right sides holding two bars and a rising line. Used for charts that plot two measures with different scales, such as sales and margin.

chart-half-donut.context: A semicircular ring split into three segments with flat ends at the bottom. Used for compact share charts, gauge style progress and election result summaries.

chart-nested-donut.context: Two concentric rings, each broken into arc segments at different angles. Used for comparing two related breakdowns, such as this year and last year, in one round chart.

parliament-chart.context: Small seat markers arranged in two curved rows forming a semicircle above a base line. Used for showing how seats are divided among parties after an election.

chart-proportional-area.context: Three squares of increasing size, a small solid one and two outlined ones, sitting on a shared baseline. Used for comparing magnitudes by area in infographics.

chart-small-multiples.context: A two by two grid of small frames, each holding a tiny line graph with a different shape. Used for comparing the same chart across several groups at a glance.

chart-radial-tree.context: A central dot with lines out to three child dots, each branching again to two outer dots. Used for showing hierarchies that spread out from one root in all directions.

chart-positive-negative.context: A horizontal zero line with a solid hump above it on the left and an outlined dip below it on the right. Used for data that swings between gains and losses, such as profit or temperature anomalies.

chart-annotation.context: A line chart with one point marked by a dot and a small note box above it pointing down at the point. Used for adding comments, insights or event labels to charts.

chart-drilldown.context: One tall outlined bar on the left with dashed lines leading to three smaller bars on the right. Used for exploring a total by opening it into its parts.

chart-forecast.context: A solid line rising across the chart that continues as a dashed line inside a widening cone. Used for forecasts, projections and predictions with growing uncertainty.

chart-moving-average.context: A jagged zigzag line with a smooth curve running through the middle of it. Used for smoothing noisy data to reveal the underlying trend, such as in stock or sales charts.

goal-thermometer.context: A thermometer shaped tube filled about two thirds of the way up, with tick marks beside it. Used for fundraising goals, donation drives and campaign progress trackers.

chart-period-comparison.context: Two lines over the same corner axis: a solid line for this period above a dashed line for the previous period. Used for year over year and month over month comparisons.

break-even-chart.context: A corner axis with a steep revenue line crossing a flatter cost line, the crossing marked with a dot. Used in business planning to find the point where income covers costs.

supply-demand-curve.context: Two curves crossing in an X over a corner axis, one rising and one falling, with a dot where they meet. Used in economics to show market equilibrium price and quantity.

long-tail-distribution.context: A curve that drops steeply from a high start and trails off in a long flat tail, above bars that shrink the same way. Used for niche markets, popularity and power law data.

s-curve.context: A corner axis with an S shaped curve that starts flat, rises steeply in the middle and levels off. Used for adoption curves, logistic growth and project progress plans.

exponential-growth.context: A corner axis with a curve that stays nearly flat and then shoots up steeply at the right, like a hockey stick. Used for rapid growth, compounding and viral spread.

normal-distribution.context: A symmetrical bell curve above a baseline with a vertical line under its peak. Used in statistics for the normal distribution, averages and grading curves.

skewed-distribution.context: A lopsided hill curve above a baseline, with its peak toward the left and a long tail to the right. Used for data that is not symmetrical, such as incomes or waiting times.

bimodal-distribution.context: A curve with two humps of similar height separated by a dip, above a baseline. Used for data with two common values or two groups mixed together.

standard-deviation.context: A capital sigma sign above a bell curve that is divided into bands by vertical lines on both sides of its centre. Used for standard deviation, variance and spread in statistics.
